paper_title: High-Efficiency Large-Bandgap Material for Polymer Solar Cells
source_file: /home/wzfeng/MySearch/PhotoRag/MD/Macromolecular Rapid Communications - 2014 - Wei - High‐Efficiency Large‐Bandgap Material for Polymer Solar Cells/auto/Macromolecular Rapid Communications - 2014 - Wei - High‐Efficiency Large‐Bandgap Material for Polymer Solar Cells.md

knowledge_points.content: HD-PDFc-DTBT is synthesized via Suzuki polycondensation using N-(2-hexyldecyl)-3,6-difluorocarbazole as the donor unit, 5,6-bis(octyloxy)benzothiadiazole as the acceptor unit, and thiophene as a spacer.
knowledge_points.evidence: High-molecular-weight conjugated polymer HD-PDFc-DTBT with N-(2-hexyldecyl)-3,6-difluorocarbazole as the donor unit, 5,6-bis(octyloxy)benzothiadiazole as the acceptor unit and thiophene as the spacer is synthesized by Suzuki polycondensation.

knowledge_points.content: Replacing the octyl chain with a branched 2-hexyldecyl chain at the 9-position of the carbazole unit in HD-PDFc-DTBT increases the polymer's solubility, allowing for the synthesis of higher molecular weight materials (Mn = 38.3 kg/mol) compared to its predecessor O-PDFC-DTBT (Mn = 9.1 kg/mol).
knowledge_points.evidence: In this work, to achieve high-molecular-weight polymers, we replace the octyl chain on the 9-position of 3,6-difluorocarbazole unit with a 2-hexyldecyl chain to increase the solubility of the resulting polymers... Number-average molecular weight of HD-PDFC-DTBT has reached 38.3 kg mol-1.

knowledge_points.content: HD-PDFc-DTBT exhibits a large optical bandgap of 1.96 eV and a high hole mobility of 0.16 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ in organic field-effect transistors (OFETs).
knowledge_points.evidence: HD-PDFC-DTBT shows a large bandgap of 1.96 eV and a high hole mobility of 0.16 cm2 V−1 s−1.

knowledge_points.content: Inverted polymer solar cells based on HD-PDFc-DTBT:PC71BM (1:3 weight ratio) achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 7.39% with a Voc of 0.93 V, a Jsc of 14.11 mA cm⁻², and an FF of 0.56.
knowledge_points.evidence: When C-PCBSD was used as the interfacial layer, the PCE was further enhanced to 7.39% with a Voc of 0.93 V, a Jsc of 14.11 mA cm−2, and an FF of 0.56.

knowledge_points.content: The hole mobility of HD-PDFc-DTBT (0.16 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹) is approximately 50 times higher than that of its lower molecular weight analog, O-PDFC-DTBT (3.1 × 10⁻³ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹), which is attributed to the increased molecular weight.
knowledge_points.evidence: HD-PDFC-DTBT film exhibited a very promising p-type transistor performance, with saturated charge carrier mobilities up to 0.16 cm2 V−1 s−1 observed, a factor of 50 larger than the mobility obtained from O-PDFC-DTBT film (3.1 × 10−3 cm2 V−1 s−1).

knowledge_points.content: The use of a cross-linked fullerene derivative, C-PCBSD, as an interfacial electron-transfer layer between the ZnO and the active layer increases the PCE of HD-PDFc-DTBT devices from 6.95% to 7.39%.
knowledge_points.evidence: The cross-linking C-PCBSD film can be used as an interfacial material as an electron-transfer layer between the active layer and ZnO, which can significantly improve the performance of PSCs. When C-PCBSD was used as the interfacial layer, the PCE was further enhanced to 7.39%.

knowledge_points.content: UV-vis absorption spectra of HD-PDFc-DTBT in chlorobenzene show strong aggregation at room temperature, indicated by well-resolved peaks at 534 and 573 nm, which disappear and blue-shift to a single peak at 524 nm when heated to 80 °C.
knowledge_points.evidence: When the polymer solution was heated to 80 °C, the absorption spectrum was markedly blue-shifted, and the two well-resolved peaks in the low-energy region disappeared and a new featureless broad absorption peak appeared at 524 nm... the polymer chains of HD-PDFC-DTBT formed a strong aggregation in solution at room temperature.

knowledge_points.content: Optimal device performance for HD-PDFc-DTBT:PC71BM was achieved using 1,2-dichlorobenzene (DCB) as the processing solvent without the need for processing additives.
knowledge_points.evidence: Figure 3 shows the best device performance with a blend film of HD-PDFC-DTBT:PC71BM in an optimal weight ratio of 1:3 spin-coated from DCB solution as the active layer... It is worth noting that the good performance was achieved without using any processing additive.

knowledge_points.content: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) of the HD-PDFc-DTBT:PC71BM blend films reveals an interpenetrated bicontinuous network that facilitates efficient exciton dissociation and charge transport with low recombination.
knowledge_points.evidence: TEM image suggests that interpenetrated networks for electron and hole transport have been formed. Such ideal interpenetrating network would provide a suitable interface between the polymer and the PC71BM and ensure efficient exciton dissociation.

knowledge_points.content: Fluorination of the carbazole unit in HD-PDFc-DTBT results in deeper HOMO (-5.32 eV) and LUMO (-3.30 eV) energy levels compared to non-fluorinated analogs, which contributes to a high open-circuit voltage (Voc) in solar cell devices.
knowledge_points.evidence: HOMO energy level of HD-PDFC-DTBT was calculated to be −5.32 eV... LUMO energy level of HD-PDFC-DTBT was calculated to be −3.30 eV... It is apparent that the fluoro-substituted polymers are of deeper HOMO and LUMO energy levels than the corresponding nonfluorosubstituted polymers, which is beneficial to achieving high Voc for devices.
